e-8761.knowledge_point: Graphing a Stretched Negative Reciprocal Function
e-8761.worked_solution:
To plot $y = -\dfrac{1}{5x},$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\dfrac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/d5d93e12275c683e0a56f0ec9a0c99540a7774879cd0f8fa69151ddba68a44fa.png)

- Stretch the result by a scale factor of $\dfrac 1 5$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{1}{5x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/30ace3126ec127b9949ebf599d615020b9770458825d22460e9e7e0b3d5efec3.png)

e-5924.worked_solution:
To plot $y = -\dfrac{2}{x-1}-1,$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\dfrac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/9da0db2e6c97e507e82b7ca801e46802fabf91ad31ff53ad3cc9ae580151370a.png)

- Translate it by one unit to the right to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{1}{x-1}.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/8ce8c53f202f04b3b34a247b797f65f7616e8772afa1751de126ddd401417bd7.png)

Notice that the vertical asymptote is now $x=1.$

- Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{2}{x-1}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/c9b708a20d9c6c12f0016279e8d7a3ea55597e7645f0a9518f1c32e8a8406e47.png)

- Finally, translate it by $1$ unit down to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{2}{x-1}-1.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/e100b552adb71cae1295492a58b0e60525813adb87d9815ba64a151a856f0c46.png)

Notice that the horizontal asymptote is now $y=-1.$
